description.narrative: Access to safe and reliable water remains a critical need in Sierra Leone, particularly in areas where existing water sources are either inadequate or unsafe for daily use. In response to this urgent need, CAFOD has allocated £6,269 to support the construction of a borehole for the Archbishop. This intervention aims to provide a sustainable and dignified water supply solution that will directly improve the well-being, health, and livelihoods of people who will be accessing water from this source who currently face significant challenges accessing clean water. The project will be implemented by Caritas Freetown, leveraging its strong local presence, technical experience, and established community engagement structures. The funds will support the full process of drilling and installing a borehole, guided by technical cost estimates currently being finalized in consultation with Caritas Freetown. Once completed, the borehole will serve as a long-term, Caritas-managed resource that enhances public health, reduces the burden of water collection on women and children, and strengthens the resilience of the target community. This initiative reflects CAFOD’s ongoing commitment to supporting life-saving basic services, promoting human dignity, and accompanying the local Church in responding to essential needs of the Church.
